summary: New box Infectum: example for sense 1 in Infectum (Jan 2.27/4542)

data.turoyo: I naqqa d kməṭwaṣlo i ǧamaʕa, ḥa lə kəbʕe d ṭowər i ǧamaʕa.
data.translation: When the community joins together, one does not want to break up the community.

rationale: First Detransitive sense and Infectum box for II; explicit collective subject and contrast with breaking up the community.
An unprefixed motion form has the arriving participant as subject and l gabe as goal. It contrasts with the inherited II causative; only the Preterit base is attested.

kməṭwaṣlo has the community as subject, no causer, and contrasts with ṭowər i ǧamaʕa. It supplies the joining counterpart of II attaching/making arrive; one attestation, subject collective, no separate arrival or reciprocal subsense inferred.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit Intransitive (53/155)

data.turoyo: Madəllalle, ayko yo. Kəzze waṣəl l gabe.
data.translation: Man zeigte ihm den Weg zu dem Ort, wo er war. Er ging und gelangte zu ihm.

rationale: First stem I and Preterit Intransitive example, distinct from the existing II “make arrive/attach”.

summary: 53/155 establishes I waṣəl with the arriver as subject and goal l gabe. There is no causative agent or separate transported patient, unlike the existing II gelangen lassen.
The new stem is accepted on one clear lexical and constructional attestation. Its base pair records waṣəl and an explicit gap for Infectum; no unattested paradigm member is supplied.

The preceding kəzze followed by bare waṣəl gives a motion sequence. The entry places the bare qaṭəl event form under Preterit Intransitive; the German past is supporting context rather than the basis for the box.
Preserve inherited II forms, sense numbering and examples. The arrival stem does not justify separating the inherited attachment and caused-arrival glosses in this run.
No light-verb idiom or participant extension requires a separate note.

wəṣəlna in Jan 2.10/2285 belongs to a quoted Arabic clause (Nəḥne ... li baladkən ... anta ... naḥnu nsaʕədək). It cannot supply a Turoyo active Preterit box or a productive first-person form. Round 1 I.1 remains based on its Turoyo evidence only.
The community subject of kməṭwaṣlo gives an agentless collective joining event. Reciprocal versus collective self-organization cannot be separated from a single feminine collective subject.
Retain source ṭ in məṭwaṣlo without silently normalizing it to t; no new base pair is reconstructed from one Detransitive token.
Jan English is the project machine translation, not an edition translation. It is reproduced only as supplied and is not evidence for senses; all semantic decisions rest on the Turoyo.
Confirm the productive Infectum base and the inflectional status of this Arabic-derived I form. The single token does not establish a complete Preterit/Infectum pair.
Is I waṣəl ordinary across dialects or restricted to this narrative/contact register?
Confirm kməṭwaṣlo as the Turoyo II Detransitive formation and the source ṭ/t variation, rather than an unintegrated Arabic reciprocal form.
Does the community predicate denote gathering on an occasion or maintaining communal connection? The proposed gloss covers joining without asserting duration.
